title: .recomp.json
description: What a recompilation or decompilation project says about itself, in a file at the root of its own repository. Specification: https://recomp.fyi/spec. Licence: CC BY 4.0, recomp.board.

^x-.description: Extensions for one reader or tool. Readers that do not know them ignore them.

$schema.description: https://recomp.fyi/schema/v1.json lets editors check the file and complete field names.

game.description: The game's title as it shipped.

wikidata.description: The game's Wikidata item (Q followed by digits). Lets any database match the game without guessing from the title.

system.description: The platform of the original binary the project works from (recompiled, decompiled, or ported from its decompiled source), not where the result runs. A re-release on another console is that console. For a port of source code its authors released, the platform that source was written for. A list when the project works from several. Suggested spellings: https://recomp.fyi/spec#names

type.description: recomp: static recompilation of the original binary. port: a source port, the game built natively from decompiled, disassembled or rewritten source code, an engine rewritten from the game's file formats included. decomp: source code rebuilt from the binary. A list when one repository delivers two of them.

original.description: The release of the game the project works from: the one a user must own. One object, or a list when several are supported. Never a file or a link to one.

status.description: exploring: feasibility, no promises. in-progress: actively worked on. playable: runs start to finish, rough edges remain. released: public build, still maintained. complete: finished, a decomp whose source fully rebuilds the original or a recomp or source port with no further work planned. paused: on hold. unknown means the same as leaving the field out.

targets.description: Where the project's build runs. A console is written with its system name. Suggested spellings: https://recomp.fyi/spec#names

toolchain.description: The recompiler or decomp toolkit the project is built on; for a source port, the engine or layer it is built on. Not the decompilation a source port starts from: the type says that, and its address belongs in links. A list when the project is built on several.

links.description: Devlog, Discord, forum thread. Never a game file or where to get one.

help.description: Short phrases, one per thing the project would welcome a hand with.

notes.description: Free text: what works, what is next.

revision.description: The release's revision as the community names it.

serial.description: Product code printed on the disc, cartridge or box, or shown on the store page.

sha1.description: SHA-1 of the file the project expects, so a user can check their own copy.
